query: The Dummy Hits Back The eyepatched dummy has started throwing hexes back. Lyra splits its seam and pulls out an old captain's charm, sewn in decades ago and still humming. "It empties if someone holds firm in the circle while it fires," she says. "Nobody's managed it. Nobody's tried properly." "I'll try properly." Lyra sews the charm back in, looks at you, and writes your name on the board under the dummy. Underneath, someone adds a small drawing of a stretcher. Leave it to the seniors You go back to your bout, and the dummy goes back to hexing whoever passes. A senior limps past at the end of practice, still smoking slightly.
